about: The one config file. Every threshold and rule number used by the pages in app/ and by the Python scripts in analysis/ lives here, with the spec section it comes from. 'source' says where the number came from: 'spec' = stated in docs/SPEC.md; 'research' = stated in the research report where the spec is silent; 'draft' = an engineering starting value of this build, to be tuned from real recordings. Every value is adjustable: change it here and both the pages and the analysis pick it up.

capture.echoCancellation.note: Requested off when the microphone opens. What the iPad actually grants is logged.

capture.channelCount.note: One channel is asked for; the first channel is recorded whatever is granted.

capture.wavBitDepth.note: Uncompressed PCM. 16 bits keeps a session file near 200 MB; 32 (float) is also supported.

capture.chunkFrames.note: How many samples the recorder hands over at a time.

capture.exportPartMaxMB.note: Size of each file when a session is exported in parts instead of as one file.

capture.clipLevel.note: A sample at or above this counts as clipped; clipped takes are flagged.

script.sessionsMin.note: At least three sessions on different days, so whole sessions can be held out.

script.chordsMin.note: Eight to twelve chords he will use.

script.chordsMax.note: Eight to twelve chords he will use.

script.defaultChordIds.note: Ticked by default: the seven rotation chords (section 1) plus E from stage 2 (section 4). The Am shape is his choice (section 13); 5-2-0-0 is ticked first only because the spec lists it first.

script.cleanStrums.note: Clean strums per chord per session.

script.dampedCourseStrums.note: Strums with each course damped in turn. The spec gives no count; the research plan gives 10.

script.fretOffStrums.note: Strums with one finger a fret off, shared equally across the wrong shapes below.

script.fretOffVariants.note: How many different one-finger-off shapes are recorded per chord per session.

script.pairStringDampedStrums.note: Strums with one string of a pair damped. Expected to be undetectable; recorded to confirm.

script.strumCueIntervalSec.note: Time between strum cues in the single-chord takes.

script.leadInSec.note: Count-down before the first cue of a take.

script.tailSec.note: Recording continues this long after the last cue.

script.cleanDynamicsCycle.note: Clean strums are asked for at mixed dynamics.

script.cleanStrokeCycle.note: Clean strums alternate down and up.

script.changePairs.note: Pairs for the chord-change takes. A pair is only recorded if both chords are in the session's chord set.

script.clickRoutes.note: Click conditions for the chord-change takes.

script.changeBeatsPerChord.note: One strum per beat, four beats per chord (first rung of the beats-per-chord ladder).

script.changeChordSegments.note: Chords per change take: A B A B A B A B gives seven changes.

script.clickOnlyClicksPerTempo.note: Speaker click with no playing, at each tempo: 102 clicks in all, so 'false onsets per 100 clicks' can be measured.

script.speakerComparisonSound.note: A few speaker-click change takes are repeated with this other click sound, so the two can be compared while playing.

script.speakerComparisonPairs.note: Which pairs get that repeat (at every tempo).

script.clickOnlySounds.note: The speaker click with no playing is recorded once with each sound, so the recordings show which one the speaker route can live with.

script.noiseFloorSec.note: Room silence recorded at the start of a session.

script.openCoursePicks.note: Each open course is picked this many times so the session's real tuning can be measured.

metronome.lookaheadMs.note: Clicks falling inside this window are scheduled on the audio clock.

metronome.timerMs.note: How often the Web Worker timer wakes the scheduler.

metronome.minBpm.note: Lower end of the tempo range in the acceptance tests.

metronome.maxBpm.note: Upper end of the tempo range in the acceptance tests.

metronome.sound.note: Which click the metronome plays: 'woodblock' (his choice, 16 Nov 2026) or 'tick' (a short high click above the analysis band, as the research proposed for the speaker). See docs/DECISIONS.md.

metronome.woodblockAccentHz.note: Pitch of the woodblock on beat one of each bar.

metronome.woodblockOvertoneRatio.note: The woodblock's second, shorter-lived partial, as a multiple of its pitch.

metronome.woodblockOvertoneLevel.note: Loudness of that second partial against the first.

metronome.woodblockDecayMs.note: How quickly the woodblock dies away.

metronome.woodblockDurationMs.note: Total length of the woodblock sound.

metronome.clickFrequencyHz.note: The 'tick' sound: it sits above the 180 Hz to 5 kHz analysis band so it can be told apart from the strings.

metronome.accentFrequencyHz.note: The 'tick' on beat one of each bar.

metronome.clickDurationMs.note: Length of the 'tick': a short click of 10 to 20 ms.

analysis.bandLowHz.note: Lower edge of the band the analysis listens in.

analysis.bandHighHz.note: Upper edge of the band the analysis listens in.

analysis.referenceA4Hz.note: Pitch standard, before the session's measured tuning is applied.

onset.frameMs.note: Length of each analysis frame (1024 samples at 48 kHz).

onset.bandsPerOctave.note: Width of the log-spaced bands the flux is summed over.

onset.mergeWindowMs.note: Onset candidates closer than this are merged.

onset.minIntervalMs.note: Shortest gap between two reported strums.

onset.thresholdWindowMs.note: How far back the adaptive threshold looks.

onset.thresholdFactor.note: The flux must exceed this many times its recent median.

onset.thresholdFloor.note: The flux must also exceed this fixed amount.

onset.lookaheadFrames.note: Frames of look-ahead for peak picking; this is the detector's built-in delay.

onset.levelGateDb.note: A strum must rise this far above the session's noise floor.

onset.backdateWindowMs.note: How far back from the detection the true start of the strum is searched for.

onset.backdateRiseFraction.note: The strum is dated to where its level first passes this fraction of its rise.

onset.fluxLagFrames.note: Each frame is compared with the frame this many steps earlier.

onset.envelopeMs.note: Smoothing of the level curve used to date the start of a strum.

onset.referenceMinRise.note: Offline yardstick only: how sharply the level must jump, added over a few wide bands, for a strum to be counted as played.

timing.matchToleranceMs.note: A detected onset within this of a true onset counts as found.

timing.gradeBandMs.note: Timing is graded in bands no finer than about 40 to 50 ms.

chord.windowStartMs.note: The chord check listens from this long after the onset.

chord.windowEndMs.note: ... to this long after the onset.

chord.partials.note: Partials 1 to 4 or 5 of each course's expected note.

chord.bandCents.note: Half-width of the band around each expected partial (25 to 30 cents).

chord.profileBandsPerOctave.note: Resolution of the calibrated profile each strum is compared with.

chord.calibrationStrums.note: Two or three clean strums of each chord make the session's calibrated profile.

chord.minSnrDb.note: Below this level above the noise floor the verdict is 'couldn't tell'.

chord.tuneQuantilePct.note: When thresholds are tuned, each rule is set so that this share of clean training strums would break it.

chord.safetyMarginDb.note: Extra slack added to each tuned threshold, in favour of calling a strum clean.

chord.uncertainMarginDb.note: A strum that breaks a rule by less than this is 'couldn't tell', not 'not clean'.

chord.safetySimilarity.note: Extra slack added to the tuned similarity threshold, in favour of calling a strum clean.

chord.uncertainSimilarity.note: A strum this close below the similarity threshold is 'couldn't tell', not 'not clean'.

chord.profileCompression.note: Band energies are raised to this power before strums are compared with the profile, so loud and soft strums look alike.

chord.neighbourGuardCents.note: A wrong-note band is ignored if it lies this close to a partial the chord is expected to have.

chord.minWindowMs.note: If the next strum arrives so soon that less than this is left to listen to, the verdict is 'couldn't tell'.

chord.fftOversample.note: Zero-padding of the spectrum, so narrow bands around each partial can be read.

chord.defaultAbsentDropDb.note: Before tuning: a course this far below its calibrated level counts as missing.

chord.defaultNeighbourRiseDb.note: Before tuning: energy this far above normal a fret away from an expected note counts as a wrong note.

chord.defaultInChordDropDb.note: Before tuning: allowed fall in the ratio of in-chord to out-of-chord energy.

chord.defaultMinSimilarity.note: Before tuning: lowest similarity to the calibrated profile.

bar.majorityOf.note: Scoring is per bar by majority; uncertain strums are left out.

pass.falseRejectMaxPct.note: Clean strums wrongly rejected, per strum, on sessions held out from tuning.

pass.falseAcceptDifferentNotesMaxPct.note: Wrong chords accepted: a different note set.

pass.falseAcceptFretOffMaxPct.note: Wrong chords accepted: one finger a fret off.

pass.missingCourseFalseAlarmMaxPct.note: ... at this many false alarms or fewer.

pass.onsetFMin.note: Strum onsets found, within the match tolerance.

pass.firstCleanStrumFoundMinPct.note: First clean strum found, share of changes.

pass.computeRealTimeFractionMax.note: Analysis at a quarter of real time or less.

pass.stopRuleFalseRejectPct.note: Stop rule: if false rejects stay above about this after tuning, nothing is gated on chord verdicts.

device.loopbackClicks.note: Clicks played and listened for in one latency measurement (8 to 16).

device.tempoHoldBpms.note: Tempos for the metronome hold check (acceptance test: 60 to 200 bpm).

device.dataSurvivalDays.note: Data survival after two weeks unused.

device.tunerWindowSamples.note: Window for the pitch readout used in the tuner-accuracy check.

device.tunerClarityMin.note: Clarity gate: readings below this are not shown.

device.clickFoundMinRatio.note: A click counts as heard when its match peak is this many times the background.

device.clickSearchAfterMs.note: How long after its scheduled time a click is looked for. A longer round trip (Bluetooth, say) shows as not heard.

device.clickSearchSpacingShare.note: The search for a click stops this share of the way to the next click.

device.loopbackStartDelayMs.note: Pause between starting to record and the first click.

device.loopbackTailMs.note: Recording continues this long after the last click.

device.tonePurityBandPct.note: Half-width of the band counted as the tone when its purity is measured.

device.toneHeardMinPurityDb.note: Below this the tone or hiss counts as not heard by the microphone.

device.noiseDurationSec.note: Length of the hiss burst that shows whether the highs survive playback.

device.settleAfterOpenMs.note: Pause after the microphone opens before measuring.

device.promptWaitHintMs.note: A wait longer than this for the microphone suggests a permission prompt was on screen.

device.tempoHoldWaitChoicesSec.note: Optional wait before the tempo check, so the screen can dim first.

device.tunerMinHz.note: Lowest pitch the readout looks for.

device.tunerMaxHz.note: Highest pitch the readout looks for.

device.tunerPeakPick.note: McLeod pitch method: the first peak at least this share of the highest is taken.

device.tunerHopSamples.note: New samples between pitch readings (about six readings a second at 48 kHz).

device.tunerDisplayReadings.note: The display shows the middle of this many recent readings.

device.tunerLogWindowMs.note: A logged reading is the middle of the readings in this last stretch.

device.tunerMaxCentsFromCourse.note: A reading further than this from the chosen open course is refused.
